concurrency_note: check_traceability is a single-pass static text scan of epic docs + a checked-in source tree at a fixed SHA — there is no concurrent/racing dimension in the artifact to evade.

authority_boundary.proves: every stable-ID contract/invariant carries a code @cw-trace guards/ensures annotation (coverage) and a test/probe/policy/telemetry @cw-trace verifies annotation (tested), every BR has an incoming realizes from a defined contract/invariant, and every @cw-trace annotation targets a defined ID with a schema-valid verb/source-kind pairing — over the file extensions the scanner walks (.py/.go/.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.java/.rb/.rs/.rego/.yaml/.yml); and — as of chief-wiggum#281 — that the scanner ACTUALLY PARSED the epic's stable IDs: an epic whose ID-bearing artifacts carry content but yield zero parseable IDs reports applicability=error (not a green `inapplicable`), names the malformed near-miss tokens with file:line, and exits non-zero under BOTH --gate soundness and --gate coverage; and — as of #282 — that every file in the scanned population was actually READ: a file the scanner could not decode or open is named in `unscanned` rather than silently dropped, so a zero finding count is no longer ambiguous between 'nothing wrong' and 'nothing read'; and - as of #313 - that a sidecar external-link store which is POPULATED but anchors nothing is reported as error and blocks, rather than surfacing as warnings that never satisfy coverage. For a C#-on-sidecar target the link store is the ONLY route to coverage (C# is tier 2 and CW emits no guard scaffolds for it), so before this the coverage gate was permanently unsatisfiable there
authority_boundary.artifact: a git worktree copy of the target repo's epic docs (docs/epics/<slug>) plus its tracked source tree
assumptions: an @cw-trace annotation is trusted as accurate by presence — the checker verifies the tag exists, not that the annotated code/test actually implements the guard/verification it claims to
only annotations that appear as literal text on a single line are found; a dynamically-constructed or multi-line-split annotation is invisible to the regex
only the listed file extensions are scanned; an annotation placed in an unscanned extension (e.g. .txt, .md outside the epic doc tree) does not count toward coverage

the error state distinguishes a BROKEN INSTRUMENT from an EMPTY SUBJECT by content, not by mere presence: an ID-bearing artifact that is absent, zero-byte or whitespace-only is still `inapplicable` (nothing was authored yet), while one carrying content that yields no parseable IDs is `error`

near-miss detection is the grammar's complement, not a heuristic — it flags only declaration-position tokens whose KIND is real but whose shape is not KIND-SLUG-NNN. A token that merely starts with a valid ID and continues with a hyphenated suffix (e.g. the sub-id CTR-order-confirm-001-pre1) is deliberately NOT flagged; that exemption was derived from a false positive found in the #281 precision dry-run, not assumed

what this does NOT prove: that the ids the scanner parsed are the RIGHT ids, or that a parseable epic is a complete one — only that a silently-unparseable epic can no longer be mistaken for a clean one

a mildly-corrupt file is scanned LOSSILY rather than skipped (utf-8 errors='replace'): a replacement character cannot fabricate a write site or an annotation, so a lossy read can yield a false negative but never a false positive

what this does NOT prove: that a lossily-decoded file was fully understood — only that it was not silently dropped. A file decoding to >30% replacement characters is reported unscanned instead of scanned-as-garbage
BOM-less UTF-16 is detected by NUL-byte interleaving density, not by a BOM or a replacement-character ratio — the ratio for that case is 0%, which is precisely why it went undetected in the first cut

the external-link store's applicability follows the same line as every other input: ZERO entries is 'inapplicable' (nothing authored yet), entries that exist but none of which anchor is 'error'. This is a SECOND instance of the instrument-broken class rather than a new class - the store is an instrument that ran and saw nothing - and that class already carries a genuinely-passing seeded trial (tr-instrument-broken-01). Its specific blocking path is verified live by the check_traceability integration test added in #313, which asserts --gate coverage returns 1 with applicability 'error' on a fully-unresolved store
